question: What pushed Britain into controlling rents in 1915, in the middle of a world war?
answer: A rent strike in Glasgow. As munitions workers crowded in, landlords raised rents; by late 1915 around 20,000 tenants refused to pay the increases, led largely by women such as Mary Barbour. With shipyard output at stake, Parliament froze rents at pre-war levels within weeks. Some form of rent control lasted over seventy years.
move: Emergency rules outlive emergencies when enough people come to depend on them.
ask: Which temporary rule have I come to depend on, and will it outlive its emergency?
